hypothesis: Light eth_call is wakeup-bound; leaving C6/C6P costs 170-210us on c8i and C2 100us on c8a. Disabling idle states with exit latency above 1us (keeps POLL and C1) should cut wakeup latency on x86. c8g exposes no cpuidle states, so it doubles as a control there.
llm_commentary: Disabling CPU idle states with exit latency above 1us (on-box: c8a C2=1; c8i C1E/C6/C6P=1; POLL and C1 kept) cut c8a from the same-boot control's 5.12s [5.08-5.14] to 4.56s [4.51-4.59], -10.9%. That is the largest single instance-level lever so far and fits the profile: light eth_call is a stream of cross-thread wakeups, and a worker parked in C2 (100us exit latency) adds that to each handoff it receives. c8i is within noise (5.49→5.45s) despite C6's 170-210us latency, which suggests Granite Rapids vCPUs here rarely reach C6 under this load or the hypervisor masks it; c8g exposes no cpuidle states (control, 6.41→6.43s). This boot's c8a host was ~10% slower than earlier ones (control 5.12s vs 4.67s), so a closing control run on the same boot will confirm the effect is not drift; if it holds, the faster earlier c8a hosts may simply have been entering C2 less.
